The session to ride for a comparison

Source: R/protocol.R
comparison_protocol.Rd

The block-by-block protocol from vignette("recording_rides"), as data. Each row is one interval: how long, whether the trainer should hold the target, and what the target is as a fraction of FTP.

Usage

comparison_protocol(step_seconds = 120, surges = 4)

Arguments

step_seconds

Seconds per ladder step. The binding constraint is not min_seconds but how many bootstrap blocks each band carries: the up and down ladders land in the same bands, so a band holds roughly 2 * step_seconds, and the default 120 gives it about four 60-second blocks. Going shorter drops under three, and resampling two blocks is not an estimate. Lengthening to 240 buys about 17% narrower bands for twice the ladder.

surges

Number of coast-to-power edges in the sync block.

Value

A tibble of block, seconds, mode, target_pc, cue and why, one row per interval, in riding order. cue is what the rider is told at the time; why is what the block is for.

Details

Each block exists for something the pipeline needs, and why carries the reason:

  • The sync surges are not there to find the offset — when the app records, one clock stamps every sample and the offset is zero by construction. They are there because align_rides() cannot tell "these clocks agree" from "these traces cannot be compared at all" and collapses both into unresolved. Without an edge to lock onto, a recorder that stamped every meter wrongly passes exactly as a correct one does.

  • The ladder puts a chosen number of seconds into each band, because agreement_by_level() only has a band if you spent time in it.

  • The ladder runs up and then back down because a meter reading high through warming up gives different numbers at the same target on the way down, where a level-dependent meter repeats itself. Ridden one way only, level_dependence() cannot separate them.

mode is "erg" where the trainer holds the target and "free" where it must not: a trainer in erg fights a surge and rounds off the very edge the sync block exists to provide.

There is one sync block, at the front, and no second one at the end. A closing block would only detect a clock drifting during the ride, and when the app records there is one clock stamping every meter — it cannot drift relative to itself, so the block would cost the best part of two minutes to rule out something that cannot happen. Independent head units are a different case, where two clocks can separate; that route is prose in vignette("recording_rides") rather than this function, and it should repeat the surges at the end.

Examples

comparison_protocol()
#> # A tibble: 21 × 6
#>    block           seconds mode  target_pc cue                             why  
#>    <chr>             <dbl> <chr>     <dbl> <chr>                           <chr>
#>  1 Zero and settle      30 free       0    Zero-offset every meter, then … A sh…
#>  2 Sync surges           8 free       1.5  Out of the saddle, hard         Coas…
#>  3 Sync surges          20 free       0    Stop pedalling completely       Coas…
#>  4 Sync surges           8 free       1.5  Out of the saddle, hard         Coas…
#>  5 Sync surges          20 free       0    Stop pedalling completely       Coas…
#>  6 Sync surges           8 free       1.5  Out of the saddle, hard         Coas…
#>  7 Sync surges          20 free       0    Stop pedalling completely       Coas…
#>  8 Sync surges           8 free       1.5  Out of the saddle, hard         Coas…
#>  9 Sync surges          20 free       0    Stop pedalling completely       Coas…
#> 10 Ladder up           120 erg        0.55 Hold the target and a steady c… Seve…
#> # ℹ 11 more rows
sum(comparison_protocol()$seconds) / 60
#> [1] 23.86667
